Definition: from G5457; to shed rays, i.e. to shine or (transitively) to brighten up (literally or figuratively):--enlighten, illuminate, (bring to, give) light, make to see.
BiblicalUsage: Photizo means to enlighten, to shed rays, to bring to light, and it is the word for what Christ does to every man. John says He is the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world, and Paul prays that the eyes of our understanding may be enlightened. The writer to the Hebrews speaks of those who were once enlightened and tasted the heavenly gift, and Paul says Christ has abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe enlightenment is not a human achievement but a gift of the true Light: He lightens every man, opens the eyes of understanding, and brings immortality to light. The same light that once enlightened me can be tasted and then turned from, which is why Hebrews warns me so soberly. My position is that the light I have is meant to be walked in, not merely admired.
